edges.description: The extra Y raises the dosage of pseudoautosomal (e.g., SHOX) and Y-linked genes.

nodes.description: Presence of an extra Y chromosome, usually from paternal meiotic-II nondisjunction or a postzygotic mitotic event, raising the dosage of Y-linked and pseudoautosomal genes.

evidence.reference_title: 47,XYY syndrome: clinical phenotype and timing of ascertainment.
evidence.snippet: The XYY phenotype commonly includes tall stature, macrocephaly, macroorchidism, hypotonia, hypertelorism, and tremor.

evidence.reference_title: 47,XYY syndrome: clinical phenotype and timing of ascertainment.
evidence.snippet: There was an increased incidence of asthma, seizures, tremor, and autistic spectrum disorder (ASD) compared with the general population rates.

evidence.reference_title: Early manifestations in a cohort of children prenatally diagnosed with 47,XYY. Role of multidisciplinary counseling for parental guidance and prevention of aggressive behavior.
evidence.snippet: Language delay was detected in 8 out of 11 children older than 20 months.

nodes.description: Increased dosage of pseudoautosomal genes (notably SHOX, in the region shared by X and Y) contributes to the overgrowth/tall stature, while broader sex-chromosome dosage effects contribute to neurodevelopmental vulnerability.

evidence.reference_title: 47,XYY syndrome: clinical phenotype and timing of ascertainment.
evidence.snippet: Macrocephaly (head circumference >2 SD) was noted in 28/84 (33%), hypotonia in 57/90 (63%), clinodactyly in 47/90 (52%), and hypertelorism in 53/90 (59%).

nodes.description: Increased rates of speech/language delay, learning difficulties, and neurodevelopmental/behavioral conditions (attention problems, autism spectrum disorder), with generally normal-range intelligence.
